author: Epiphanius of Salamis
occasion: The author issues a binding testament or ordinance to the citizens, urging them not to bring images into churches or the cemeteries of the saints.
argument: Epiphanius commands the citizens to hold fast to the traditions they received and not to turn aside to the right or left. He specifically forbids bringing images into churches or the burial places of the saints, urging instead that God be kept in memory in their hearts. He extends the prohibition even to a common or ordinary house, because a Christian must not be distracted through the eyes and wanderings of the mind. Anyone who deliberately endeavors to comprehend the divine character of God's Word according to the incarnation from material colors is to be anathema.

outline.move: The testament is introduced as an ordinance to the citizens forbidding the bringing of images into churches or cemeteries.
The citizens are exhorted to keep the traditions and to remember God in their hearts rather than through images in churches or saints' cemeteries.
The prohibition is extended to a common or ordinary house, and anyone who deliberately endeavors to understand the incarnate divine character through material colors is anathematized.
